speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I am here to evaluate your newborn who is presenting with yellowish discoloration of the skin. When did you first notice the jaundice, and has it appeared to spread or worsen since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text: I will now examine the infant's sclera and abdomen to assess the extent of jaundice and check for hepatosplenomegaly. Does the baby have a good suck and swallow, and is he gaining weight appropriately? REQUEST TEST: Total and Direct Bilirubin

speaker: Doctor
text: The bilirubin levels are within the expected range for a 5-day-old, and the exclusive breastfeeding pattern is consistent with breast milk jaundice. Are there any signs of hemolysis, such as a positive Coombs test or family history of blood disorders, and is the infant feeding well with adequate wet diapers?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Yellowish discoloration of the skin. I also have Discoloration started from the face then spread to the trunk, Scleral icterus noted.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of late-onset jaundice in a thriving, exclusively breastfed infant with normal bilirubin levels is classic for breast milk jaundice. I do not require further testing as the infant is asymptomatic and feeding well. DIAGNOSIS READY: Breast milk jaundice
